messages:
Jorge: FYI seeing repeated short (100-300ms) tail latency spikes on shared-gpu pool in eu-west-1 starting ~03:10 UTC. Not full OOMs, but KV cache misses spike and p99 jumps. Logs attached below.

Maya: can you paste the pod logs / kernel dmesg? also which model + batch size?

Jorge: model=embed-1024-quant, batch=8 typical. snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T03:11:13Z inferer[pid=2412] WARN kv_cache.go:142 prefix_miss=0->12 latency_ms=230
2026-03-18T03:11:13Z runtime[pid=2401] INFO dma: dma_read_bytes=1.8GB burst_ms=45
2026-03-18T03:11:13Z kernel: nvidia-p2p: DMA stall detected on NVLink0
```

Ravi: NVLink/DMA messages + short bursts smell like a PCIe/NVLink pump from another tenant doing large memcpy loops. Could be a denser batch or fp16->int8 conversion happening in another container. Any co-located pods with hostNetwork or RDMA?

Jorge: quick check: 3 other tenants on node, one running large offline-batching job (tenant-z) with sustained host-to-device transfer. That job started around 03:00 UTC when spikes began.

Carla: what's our current mitigation set for noisy DMA? We have cpu/gpu cgroups but no PCIe bandwidth shaping AFAIK.

Maya: we have NIC egress shaping and submit-queue backpressure but not device DMA shaping. Two quick options: 1) move offending tenant to dedicated pool (fast but costs), 2) soft-throttle at runtime (limit concurrent host->device memcopies) and route heavy batchers to burstable pool.

Ravi: runtime change idea: add a token-bucket around host->device transfer calls in the GPU runtime so a single tenant can't saturate DMA lanes. Low-risk patch: throttled memcpy with per-tenant tokens. We can feature-flag it for eu-west-1.

Jorge: would help. For immediate relief can we reroute tenant-z to a dedicated reserved segment for some hours? ops-oncall: can you evict only that tenant or drain node?

ops-oncall: I can cordon the node and move tenant-z with our scheduler hints. ETA ~12m if we admit some disruption. Want me to proceed? @here? :warning:

Carla: before we drain, what's the cost delta if we temporarily pin tenant-z to a dedicated pool for 4 hours? rough estimate.

Maya: rough math: tenant-z uses 4x A100-equivalent for the job -> Dedicated burst pool cost ~ $0.60/hr per GPU => ~ $9.6 for 4 hours + small network egress. Cheap for customer SLA, but operationally manual.

Ravi: patch route also important for long-term. I can prototype token-bucket in runtime today, but it will need perf testing. If we limit host->device to ~600MB/s per tenant on NVLink it should smooth bursts without changing model quality.

Jorge: test checklist if we apply runtime throttle: 1) p99 latency for embed jobs, 2) throughput drop <=5%, 3) KV cache hit rate, 4) NVLink error logs.

Maya: + add an observability metric: dma_bytes_by_tenant + dma_burst_events. We don't currently tag that per-tenant. Small agent change.

ops-oncall: draining now to isolate: cordon node-13, migrate tenant-z -> pool-burst-4. Will post updates in ~15m.

infra-bot: scheduler: node node-13 cordoned by ops-oncall at 03:24 UTC. Migrations started.

Jorge: after migration p99 went back to baseline (~18ms) within two windows. NVLink DMA stalls dropped in kernel logs. Looks promising.

Carla: good. action items?

Maya: 1) Ravi to prototype throttled memcpy token-bucket and push canary in eu-west-1 next week. 2) Instrument dma_bytes_by_tenant metric (DevEx) 3) Ops to add an automated label-based routing rule to move heavy host->device batchers to burst pool when dma_burst_events > X.

Ravi: noted. I'll open a PR with a microbenchmark and perf numbers.

ops-oncall: creating a runbook entry for manual drain + label-based routing. Will link here.

Jorge: thanks all — reopening if it recurs. :thumbsup:
